name: Ra
role: Sun god, creator, and first king of the gods
fun_fact: Ra was said to sail across the sky in a barque and to grow visibly older as the day wore on.

name: Isis
role: Goddess of magic, motherhood, and the throne
fun_fact: Isis wears a throne on her head because her name is written with the hieroglyph for a throne.

name: Osiris
role: God of the dead and of resurrection, the rightful king
fun_fact: Osiris is usually shown as a mummified king holding a crook and flail, the tools of a shepherd and a ruler.

name: Set
role: God of disorder, the desert, and storms; Osiris's brother and rival
fun_fact: Set's sacred animal is a strange long-snouted creature that Egyptologists still cannot match to any living species.

name: Horus
role: Falcon god of kingship, son of Osiris and Isis
fun_fact: Every living pharaoh was identified with Horus, whose name was written in a falcon-topped serekh.

name: Anubis
role: Jackal-headed god of embalming and cemeteries
fun_fact: Priests who performed the embalming rites wore a jackal mask to act as Anubis himself.

name: Thoth
role: God of writing, wisdom, and reckoning
fun_fact: Thoth was credited with inventing hieroglyphs and with keeping the calendar of the gods.

name: Maat
role: Goddess of truth, order, and right conduct
fun_fact: Pharaohs were said to present Maat to the gods, a phrase that meant ruling justly.

name: Apep
role: Serpent of chaos who attacks the sun god's barque each night
fun_fact: Images of Apep were drawn on papyrus and then burned or cut up to render the serpent harmless.

name: Nephthys
role: Goddess of mourning and protection, sister of Isis and wife of Set
fun_fact: Nephthys's name means Lady of the House, and she often appears with Isis as a kite mourning Osiris.
